name: Persistent Fetal Vasculature

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Persistent Fetal Vasculature

criteria.description: Visualization of persistent hyaloid artery or fibrovascular stalk on imaging
Vitreoretinal traction or retinal folds on clinical exam or imaging
Failure of regression of fetal hyaloid vascular system confirmed by ultrasound or MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of leukocoria plus imaging evidence of persistent hyaloid artery or fibrovascular stalk
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging modalities such as ultrasound and MRI.

pathognomonic.notes: White pupillary reflex often the first presenting sign

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent hyaloid artery or fibrovascular stalk
pathognomonic.notes: Detected on imaging or clinical examination
searchTerms: persistent fetal eye artery or stalk

common.symptomName: Vision loss or decreased visual acuity
common.notes: Variable severity depending on extent of involvement
May lead to retinal folds or detachment
Misalignment of the eyes secondary to poor vision

occasional.notes: Lens opacification due to abnormal vitreous traction
Secondary glaucoma due to angle anomalies or traction
Involuntary eye movements due to poor vision

rare.notes: Developmental abnormalities of the iris and cornea

searchTerms: membrane behind the lens of eye

imaging: Ultrasound showing persistent hyaloid artery or fibrovascular stalk
MRI demonstrating persistent fetal vasculature and vitreoretinal abnormalities
genetic: Usually sporadic; rare familial cases reported with mutations in NDP or ATOH7 genes
other: Clinical examination revealing leukocoria, microphthalmia, and vitreoretinal traction

distinguishingFeatures: Lens opacity without persistent hyaloid artery
History of prematurity and oxygen therapy

redFlags: Leukocoria in a neonate or infant
Signs suggestive of intraocular tumor (e.g., retinoblastoma)
references: Hoyt CS, Taylor D. Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
American Academy of Ophthalmology. Persistent Fetal Vasculature Syndrome Preferred Practice Pattern. 2021.
